sources.title: United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNGA Res. 61/295)
sources.extract: Adopted 13 Sep 2007. r1 re-read from the saved PDF. Art. 11(1): right to maintain, protect and develop manifestations of culture, designs included. Art. 19: States consult and cooperate with Indigenous peoples through their own representative institutions to obtain free, prior and informed consent before measures that may affect them. Art. 31(1): right to maintain, control, protect and develop cultural heritage, traditional cultural expressions, designs and the IP over them. Art. 32(2): States seek consent before approving projects affecting lands or territories. Art. 33(1): right to determine their own identity or membership. Arts. 19 and 32(2) are addressed to States.

sources.title: Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act, SBC 2019, c. 44
sources.extract: Defines the Declaration as UNDRIP. s.3: government must align BC laws with it in consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples. s.4: action plan. ss.6-7: agreements with Indigenous governing bodies, including joint decision-making or consent agreements. Binds government, not private designers.

sources.title: United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act, S.C. 2021, c. 14
sources.extract: Royal Assent 21 Jun 2021. s.4: affirms the Declaration as a human-rights instrument with application in Canadian law and provides a framework for implementation. s.5: align federal laws. s.6: action plan with monitoring and review.

sources.title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada: Calls to Action
sources.publisher: Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada
sources.extract: Call 92 asks the corporate sector to adopt UNDRIP as a reconciliation framework and to (i) commit to meaningful consultation, respectful relationships and free, prior and informed consent before economic development projects, (ii) ensure equitable access to jobs, training and education and long-term sustainable benefits, (iii) educate management and staff. Addressed to the corporate sector.

sources.title: City of Vancouver UNDRIP Strategy: Report of the UNDRIP Task Force (Council item P1, 25 Oct 2022)
sources.publisher: City of Vancouver with Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations
sources.extract: NOT OPENED (HTTP 403, round 0; City domains still blocked in r1). Facts used come from S06 and S07: 79 calls to action in four themes (social, cultural and economic well-being; ending Indigenous-specific racism; self-determination and self-government; rights and title), endorsed by Council 25 Oct 2022.

sources.title: UNDRIP Task Force Celebrates Unveiling of Historic Report
sources.extract: Task Force met from 2021; report released 19 Oct 2022 and described as the first co-developed UNDRIP strategy in Canada. Co-chairs: Squamish Nation Chairperson Khelsilem and Councillor Christine Boyle. 79 calls to action under four themes. TWN councillors stress applying Coast Salish laws and revenue sharing.

sources.title: Vancouver City Council Passes Historic UNDRIP Strategy
sources.extract: Council passed the Strategy on 25 Oct 2022; 79 actions across City departments and services. r1 re-read: a new intergovernmental committee with representatives of the Host Nations, the City and urban Indigenous populations is to decide what each action requires and report back with an action plan. The release does not say whether any body other than the City is bound by the Strategy.

sources.title: City of Vancouver UNDRIP Action Plan 2024-2028
sources.extract: NOT OPENED (HTTP 403). Search-result summary only, from round 0: endorsed by Council in June 2024 and sequences a subset of 32 of the 79 actions for the first five-year phase. Verify manually.

sources.title: Musqueam Indian Band: Intergovernmental Affairs referral process
sources.extract: r1 re-read. Addressed to proponents and regulators; asks that Musqueam be contacted at the initial stages of planning for all projects within its territory. Eight package items: project description with location, schedule and activities; anticipated regulatory processes (examples: Water Sustainability Act, Fisheries Act authorization, provincial environmental assessment); archaeological or environmental studies; heritage investigation or research permit information; prior correspondence; maps; GIS files (shapefiles preferred, KMZ or KML alternative); aerial imagery. The Band may ask for more. No fees. The page does not mention academic, student or hypothetical projects, so applicability to a competition entry is not established.

sources.title: Musqueam Indian Band: Our Territory
sources.extract: Ancestors stewarded the Fraser River estuary for thousands of years. The 1976 Musqueam Declaration asserts title within a boundary running around the watershed draining into English Bay, Burrard Inlet and Indian Arm. Points to an interactive Place Names Map.

sources.title: Musqueam Place Names Map
sources.extract: Round 0 reading: interactive map with Elder audio in the hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ language, photos by location and a children's book. States that it is under review and should not be considered final. Requests go to a listed email address; site-wide copyright is the Band's. A r1 re-fetch returned HTTP 520 (transient), so this was not re-confirmed.

sources.title: Squamish Nation: Partnerships and Entities
sources.extract: Lists entities (Hiy̓ám̓ Housing, Nch'ḵay̓ Development Corporation, Squamish Nation Trust) and partnerships (MST Development Corporation, Sen̓áḵw, Squamish Lil'wat Cultural Centre). Entities and partnerships are listed separately from the Nation's government. r1: the critic reads the housing name without the mark on the y; the fetch tool read it with the mark. Orthography unresolved; a human must copy it with a codepoint check. The Squamish home page lists no referral or proponent-guidance page.

sources.title: Tsleil-Waututh Nation Sacred Trust Initiative
sources.extract: Names Burrard Inlet as səlilwət and describes it as a grandmother that has sustained the Nation. TWN's own assessment combined science with traditional TWN knowledge and rests on what it calls its unextinguished law. Shows how the Nation names and frames its place.

sources.title: Sen̓áḵw (official project site, home and About pages)
sources.extract: Two phases named Mountain Towers and Long Towers. Mountain Towers are curved, described as inspired by Coast Salish motifs, with rooftops angled north to honour the Twin Sisters; Long Towers reference longhouses with rippling screens suggesting salmon. Coast Salish artwork for the pool is by a Squamish artist. Claims net-zero carbon (developer claim, unverified). The page gives no meaning for the names Sen̓áḵw or Nch'ḵay̓ and no Squamish name for the Twin Sisters.

sources.title: Sen̓áḵw (Wikipedia)
sources.extract: Part of Kitsilano Indian Reserve No. 6; 11.7 acres returned to Squamish control. Lead says a 2001 court settlement; History says a negotiated settlement in June 2000; the page does not reconcile them. Led by Nch'ḵay̓ Development Corporation; Westbank sold its stake in Phases 1-2 to OPTrust in Aug 2025 (50/50 with the Nation; Nation holds 100% of Phases 3-4). At least 6,000 rental homes; tallest tower 58 storeys. r1: says some buildings are exempt from local height restrictions, citing a 2020 Guardian article (secondary, not opened); describes no services agreement with the City.

sources.title: Dezeen: Revery Architecture's Sen̓áḵw towers
sources.extract: Revery Architecture is design architect, Kasian architect of record. More than 11 towers of 12 to 58 storeys. Concept 'village in the park'. Copper facades chosen for cultural significance; long towers raised to create a forest-like street level. Developer says Squamish members were consulted and a Cultural Working Group was formed (developer statements).

sources.title: Jericho Lands policy statement approved by Vancouver council (Global News)
sources.extract: Council approved the policy statement on 24 Jan 2024. About 13,000 homes for roughly 24,000 people in buildings of 4 to 49 storeys over 25-30 years. Partnership of MST Development Corporation and Canada Lands Company.

sources.title: Jericho Lands policy statement draft (Storeys)
sources.extract: Draft heights peak at 26-39 storeys centrally; three 'Sentinel' buildings on the western side represent the three Nations and rise to 49 storeys; podiums to soften scale and limit impact on views and sunlight. Draft stage; subject to change.

sources.title: Policy Statement: Heather Lands
sources.extract: NOT OPENED (HTTP 403). Search-result summary from round 0: approved by Council 15 May 2018, prepared at the request of the three Nations and Canada Lands Company, covering uses, density, height, form, parks and circulation.

sources.title: MST Development Corporation (About Us and Projects)
sources.extract: Partnership of the Musqueam Indian Band, Squamish Nation and Tsleil-Waututh Nation. Full or co-owners of six Metro Vancouver properties with over 160 developable acres. Jericho west parcel owned fully or partly by the Nations; east parcel co-owned with Canada Lands Company; Heather Street Lands co-owned with CLC. States no design principles on these pages.

sources.title: CARE principles for Indigenous data (University of Auckland)
sources.extract: Four CARE principles: Collective benefit; Authority to control (Indigenous governing bodies decide how they, their lands, territories, resources, knowledge and geographical indicators are represented and identified in data); Responsibility (share how data supports self-determination); Ethics (rights and wellbeing first across the data life cycle).

sources.title: The CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance (Carroll et al.), Data Science Journal 19(1):43
sources.extract: Authored with the Global Indigenous Data Alliance. CARE complements FAIR by adding people and purpose. Informed by OCAP, which was developed in Canada in the 1990s. Sub-principle wording was not visible on the page opened.

sources.title: OCAP principles summary (University of Toronto Map and Data Library)
sources.extract: OCAP, established 1998: Ownership (collective), Control (over the whole research process), Access (Nations reach data about themselves and set rules for others), Possession (physical custody protects ownership). Applied through each Nation's own laws, review committees and agreements.

sources.title: First Nations Information Governance Centre: OCAP
sources.extract: NOT OPENED (HTTP 403 on ocap and ocap-training pages). Secondary sources say OCAP is a registered trademark of FNIGC and that FNIGC offers a Fundamentals of OCAP course. Usage conditions unverified.

sources.title: Local Contexts: Traditional Knowledge (TK) Labels
sources.extract: TK Labels let Indigenous communities state conditions for access and use. Provenance labels (e.g. TK Attribution, TK Community Voice), protocol labels (e.g. TK Culturally Sensitive, TK Secret/Sacred) and permission labels (e.g. TK Non-Commercial, TK Community Use Only). Icons and template text are copyrighted by Local Contexts.

sources.title: Local Contexts: Notices
sources.extract: r1 corrected reading. Notices are applied by institutions and researchers and their text cannot be changed. Groups: an Engagement Notice; Disclosure Notices (Attribution Incomplete, Traditional Knowledge, Biocultural); and Collections Care Notices (three icons, not named on the page). Navigation lists Hub Agreements, an API Guide, a Hub Service Schedule and Terms and Conditions, none of which were reviewed. Communities then decide whether to add their own Labels. The round 0 list of names was out of date.

sources.title: TCPS 2 (2022) Chapter 9: Research Involving the First Nations, Inuit and Metis Peoples of Canada
sources.publisher: Panel on Research Ethics (Government of Canada)
sources.extract: Art. 9.1: engage the community when research may affect its welfare, including research on cultural heritage. Art. 9.2: the form of engagement is determined jointly by researcher and community. Agreements should settle rights to knowledge and data, protect restricted knowledge and prevent unauthorized commercial use. It governs research, so it is used here by analogy.

sources.title: The International Indigenous Design Charter (ICoD news item)
sources.extract: Launched in Montreal in Oct 2017, built on the Australian Indigenous Design Charter. Self-regulated best-practice guide, open and iterative. Cited in an Australian parliamentary inquiry on inauthentic Indigenous 'style' art. The page does not list the principles. r1: the news page's description of input from North American and Maori practitioners is not supported by the charter's own contributor appendix (see S49 and the FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag).

sources.title: Indigenous Protocol and Artificial Intelligence Position Paper
sources.publisher: Indigenous Protocol and AI Working Group (hosted via Concordia University)
sources.extract: About 20 months of discussion among Indigenous participants from Aotearoa, Australia, North America and the Pacific. Guidelines are for anyone building AI ethically. Warns that data-hungry AI can expose traditional knowledge to appropriation and extraction. Publication year not confirmed on the page.

sources.title: Native Land Digital: About
sources.extract: States its maps are not official sources, does not claim to define territories, treats borders as a colonial concept, and calls the map a starting point for deeper conversations with Indigenous communities. Nations define themselves.

sources.title: City of Vancouver Open Data: View cones (protected views)
sources.extract: API read again in r1 (21 Oct 2026): 24 records, Open Government Licence - Vancouver. Description: development within the polygons is height-limited to preserve public views. Fields: view_number, view_cone_name, description, url, geometry; no height field. Present view numbers: 3.2.1-3.2.4 (Queen Elizabeth Park), 9.1, 9.2, 10, 20, 21, 22, 27.1, 27.2, 28, A, B1, B2, D, E, G1, G2, H, J1, J2, K. Absent: whole numbers 1-2, 4-8, 11-19, 23-26 and letters C, F, I, so the set may be partial. Per-view pages are on vancouver.ca (HTTP 403 to automated fetch).

sources.title: City of Vancouver Open Data: Public art
sources.extract: Open Government Licence - Vancouver. Round 0 count: 751 records. r1 API read: fields include registryid, title_of_work, artistprojectstatement, type, status, sitename, siteaddress, primarymaterial, ownership, neighbourhood, descriptionofwork, artists (a list of numeric ids, not names), yearofinstallation, geometry. No field records an artist's Indigenous identity. A text search for Coast Salish in the description returned 17 records. Records 738, 740, 741 and 744 (2017) are City Canada 150+ murals from Indigenous artists, selected through a January 2017 call judged by a panel of Indigenous artists and art professionals; three are marked no longer in place. Record 738's site is a downtown plaza with a Nation-language name, formerly Queen Elizabeth Theatre Plaza; the record does not say who named it.

sources.title: Vancouver Tall Challenge (Buildner competition page, FAQ and jury page)
sources.extract: r1 re-read. Jury of seven, including K̓esugwilakw Sierra Tasi Baker (K̓ESU+CO), per the jury page. Participants may not contact jurors; attempts mean disqualification; all communication goes to Buildner staff by the listed email or contact form. Registration closes 29 Oct 2026; Q&A deadline 3 Nov 2026; submission closes 30 Nov 2026, 23:59 London time; winners 26 Jan 2027. Entries are judged anonymously. FAQ: Buildner has no specific AI policy, advises checking the terms of the AI tool used, and says AI images should not generally be treated as the entrant's sole work without explicit permission. No statement on First Nations engagement.

sources.title: Vancouver Tall Challenge official brief (facts as supplied in the project context)
sources.publisher: Buildner with City of Vancouver and UBC SALA
sources.extract: Brief PDF itself not opened (the page's download links point to #); facts used come from the project description: jury weights (cultural context 30%), hypothetical full-block site, rotated north arrow on the site plan, labelled directions, no identifying information on boards, recommended QE Park skyline view and policy reflection. The Terms (S47) are now opened but do not restate the brief's anonymity wording.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy for Rezonings (1997)
sources.extract: NOT OPENED (HTTP 403 again in r1). Named in the VTC brief. Under review via the Higher Buildings Policy Review; whether it has been amended is unverified.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy Review (engagement document)
sources.extract: NOT OPENED (HTTP 403; the project page syc.vancouver.ca/projects/higher-buildings also returned 403 in r1). Named in the VTC brief as the review the competition feeds.

sources.title: IPTC NewsCodes: Digital Source Type vocabulary
sources.extract: Terms include trainedAlgorithmicMedia (created using generative AI), compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia (edited using generative AI), algorithmicMedia, compositeSynthetic and virtualRecording, each with a stable URI.

sources.title: C2PA Technical Specification 2.2
sources.publisher: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
sources.extract: Licensed CC BY 4.0. r1 read of chars 100,000-480,000 of about 579,000. Section 14.2: exactly one identity credential must appear in the signature headers of every manifest. Section 14.5: the signer's certificate and intermediates must be carried in the x5chain header. Section 18.16: the c2pa.metadata assertion can carry Exif fields including GPS position, with a redaction mechanism. Subject-field rules of the certificate profile and the Actions section were not read.

sources.title: Voluntary Code of Conduct on the Responsible Development and Management of Advanced Generative AI Systems
sources.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
sources.extract: Six outcomes: accountability, safety, fairness and equity, transparency, human oversight and monitoring, validity and robustness. Developers of public generative systems are expected to provide a reliable detection method for AI-generated content, watermarking being one example. Launched Sept 2023.

sources.title: EU AI Act, Article 50: Transparency obligations (unofficial text site)
sources.extract: 50(2): providers of systems generating synthetic image, audio, video or text must mark outputs in a machine-readable way. 50(4): deployers of deepfakes must disclose; disclosure of AI text on public-interest matters is not needed where a person has editorial responsibility and reviewed it. r1: the page is tagged amended, shows two versions of paragraph 7, says the article applies from 2 Aug 2026 under Art. 113, and lists a Digital Omnibus document without confirming a link. Timing is not settled. Not binding in BC; benchmark only.

sources.title: PIPEDA fair information principles
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.extract: Ten principles including identifying purposes, consent, limiting collection, limiting use, disclosure and retention, safeguards and openness.

sources.title: Personal Information Protection Act, SBC 2003, c. 63
sources.extract: Sets rules for private organizations handling personal information; personal information is information that can identify a person, excluding business contact and work product; consent is generally required for collection, use or disclosure.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology (W3C Recommendation)
sources.extract: Published 30 Apr 2013. Core classes Entity, Activity and Agent; relations wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo let provenance be exchanged as RDF.

sources.title: Mukurtu CMS: About
sources.publisher: Washington State University Center for Digital Scholarship and Curation
sources.extract: Open-source (GPL-3.0) platform for communities to manage and share digital heritage with cultural protocols as access levels, and integrated TK Labels.

sources.title: Vancouver Tall Challenge: Competition Terms and Conditions
sources.extract: As summarised by the fetch tool (clause numbers need a browser check). Cl. 5.1: submissions must not carry marks, logos or symbols identifying the author's source. Cl. 5.2 and 8.3: participants may not approach or communicate with any juror; breach means disqualification. Cl. 5.3: identity is revealed to the jury only after winners are chosen. Cl. 10.10: brief questions go through the portal (Ask the Jury), usually answered collectively. Cl. 15.1: official email comes from the organizer's domain. Cl. 4.1-4.3: originality, no infringement, image licences on request. Cl. 12.2-12.3: non-exclusive licence to the organizer; entrant keeps ownership. Cl. 4.1.4.2: evaluators consider the cultural and social context. No AI rule and no rule on Indigenous content.

sources.title: Government of Canada guidance page on the Crown's duty to consult and accommodate (title not captured)
sources.publisher: Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada
sources.extract: First 100,000 of about 207,000 characters read. The Crown (federal, provincial and territorial governments) holds the duty to consult and, where appropriate, accommodate. The page says the duty cannot be delegated to third parties; proponents may carry out procedural tasks, but the Crown keeps responsibility. Legal basis: the Supreme Court of Canada's 2004 Haida decision, under s.35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

sources.title: International Indigenous Design Charter: Protocols for sharing Indigenous knowledge in professional design practice (full book)
sources.publisher: Deakin University (hosted by the International Council of Design)
sources.extract: Read as text from the saved PDF. Copyright 2018; reproduction barred without prior written consent, so only names and paraphrases are used. Ten protocols: Indigenous led; Self-determined; Community specific; Deep listening; Indigenous knowledge; Shared knowledge; Shared benefits; Impact of design; Legal and moral; Charter implementation. Says projects must be Indigenous led and Indigenous participants are not simply to be referenced. A self-regulated guide; where it conflicts with territorial law, law prevails. Authors are from Deakin University and Indigenous Architecture and Design Victoria. Workshops listed in Australia, Denmark, Greenland and Sweden; the Montreal launch panel lists Canadian and US Indigenous panelists (including a Nisga'a architect); no Coast Salish contributor is named.

sources.title: Unicode Standard Annex 15: Unicode Normalization Forms
sources.extract: As read in r1: Unicode 18.0.0, revision 58, dated 2026-08-12. NFC is canonical decomposition followed by canonical composition. Canonically equivalent strings can differ in codepoints; normalizing both to one form lets a binary comparison decide equivalence.

sources.title: Content Authenticity Initiative: FAQ
sources.extract: Content Credentials can say who produced content, but creators are not required to include an identity; identity information should always be optional; sensitive information can be redacted later.

sources.title: Tsleil-Waututh Nation: Stewardship Work in the Territory (Treaty, Lands and Resources)
sources.extract: Describes the Treaty, Lands and Resources department's research, policy and restoration work, mainly on Burrard Inlet water quality, and links guides for industry and for governments (contents not read). States no referral steps, no proponent requirements and no named contact beyond the general contact page.

sources.title: Tsleil-Waututh Nation: Language, Culture and Protocol Department
sources.extract: The department gives cultural leadership and protocol support for Nation-led initiatives, events and partner projects, includes a Protocol Office, and prioritises hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ language revitalisation. The page describes no process for outside requests for names, artwork or acknowledgement text; the only route is the contact form.

flags.claim: Sen̓áḵw is an MST-led development (as framed in the packet scope).
flags.correction: Sen̓áḵw is a Squamish Nation project led by Nch'ḵay̓ Development Corporation, on Kitsilano Indian Reserve No. 6, with OPTrust as 50% partner in Phases 1-2. MST Development Corporation (Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh together) leads Jericho Lands and Heather Lands, with Canada Lands Company.
flags.detail: Sources: S13, S15, S16, S18, S21. Case studies must label tenure and decision authority separately for each precedent, because a Nation-controlled reserve and a City-rezoned site are not comparable approvals paths.

flags.claim: The International Indigenous Design Charter's principle list could not be retrieved, so M03 links rather than paraphrases (round 0 UNVERIFIED flag and M03 limits).
flags.correction: The full charter book is public on the ICoD site and lists ten protocols: Indigenous led; Self-determined; Community specific; Deep listening; Indigenous knowledge; Shared knowledge; Shared benefits; Impact of design; Legal and moral; Charter implementation. M03 now indexes its starter cards to these names with one-line paraphrases and a link.
flags.detail: The book is copyright 2018 and bars reproduction without written consent, so the tool names, links and paraphrases only. Protocol 1 says Indigenous stakeholders oversee creative development; protocol 4 says recognised custodians are actively involved. A design that represents Indigenous culture without such oversight departs from the charter. Verified by reading the saved PDF (S49) in r1.

flags.claim: The ICoD charter was built with input from Sami, Inuit, North American, Maori and Australian practitioners (S29 extract).
flags.correction: The contributor appendix lists research workshops in Australia, Denmark, Greenland and Sweden (Australian Indigenous students and staff, Inuit and Sami participants). The Montreal launch panel (Oct 2017) lists Canadian and US Indigenous panelists, including a Nisga'a architect. Maori practitioners appear only as designers of featured works, not as listed contributors. No Coast Salish contributor is named. Describe the charter as Australian-led with Nordic Indigenous workshop input and a North American launch panel.
flags.detail: Evidence: S49, appendix 4.2. The critic said no First Nations from Canada are named; that is also not quite right, because the launch panel names several. Either way the charter's fit with Coast Salish protocol is unestablished, and the tool says so on every charter-indexed card.

flags.claim: Referral-pack completeness against the Musqueam list is a verified metric for this entry (M01).
flags.correction: The page verifies the list of eight items, not that it applies to an ideas competition. It addresses proponents and regulators of projects with regulatory processes. Applicability to a competition entry is not established. The checklist leaves the entrant flow and survives as reference material for real projects. Default is no contact; brief questions go through the portal.
flags.detail: Evidence: S10 package item 2 lists regulatory processes (Water Sustainability Act, Fisheries Act authorization, provincial environmental assessment) and the page does not mention academic or hypothetical projects. Sending many student requests would use Nation staff time without any land-use decision.

flags.claim: Personal-data fields at export = 0 is a verified threshold based on S34 and S35 (M07).
flags.correction: Status is team_assumption. The brief (S35) was not opened. The competition page confirms only anonymous evaluation, and the Terms (S47) bar marks, logos or symbols that identify the author's source. Neither text states a rule for file metadata. A human must read the brief's anonymity clause.
flags.detail: Leak paths found in r1: contributor handles and fork authors in provenance records, the signer certificate chain that a C2PA manifest must carry (S39 sections 14.2 and 14.5), and GPS or author fields in embedded metadata (S39 section 18.16).

flags.claim: Local Contexts Notices are Open to Collaborate, Attribution Incomplete, TK, BC and Collections Care (S27 round 0 extract).
flags.correction: The current page lists an Engagement Notice, Disclosure Notices (Attribution Incomplete, Traditional Knowledge, Biocultural) and Collections Care Notices, and points to Hub Agreements, an API Guide and Terms and Conditions. M05 reads Notice types from the Hub at run time and shows link-out only until the Hub terms have been read.
flags.detail: Evidence: S27 re-read in r1.

flags.claim: The City view-cone dataset gives the full set of protected public views ('24 polygons of protected public views').
flags.correction: Treat the dataset as partial until it is checked against the City's view-protection guidelines in a browser. Zero intersections is not clearance. A touched cone still needs the City's per-view height rule, which is not in the dataset.
flags.detail: Evidence: S32 re-read in r1. Present view numbers: 3.2.1-3.2.4, 9.1, 9.2, 10, 20, 21, 22, 27.1, 27.2, 28 and A, B1, B2, D, E, G1, G2, H, J1, J2, K. Whole numbers 1-2, 4-8, 11-19, 23-26 and letters C, F, I are absent. Whether those are repealed, never existed or missing from the export is unknown.

flags.claim: Canadian Indigenous design charters published by Nations or Indigenous design bodies exist for tall-building design.
flags.correction: None found for tall buildings or for Coast Salish territory. The closest instrument is the International Indigenous Design Charter (S49), which is Australian-led.
flags.detail: Round 0 said its principle list could not be retrieved; that was wrong and is superseded by the r1 FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag. No Nation-published design guideline for downtown towers was found in r1 either.

flags.claim: City of Vancouver policy documents (UNDRIP Strategy PDF, Action Plan 2024-2028, Higher Buildings Policy 1997 and Review, Heather Lands Policy Statement, view-cone pages) say what the packet summarises.
flags.detail: All City web domains returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches in round 0 and again in r1. Facts about the 79 actions come from Tsleil-Waututh pages; the 32-of-79 figure and the Heather Lands approval date come only from search-result summaries. A teammate must open these in a normal browser before anything is cited as verified.

flags.claim: The 1997 Higher Buildings Policy is still the governing policy.
flags.detail: The brief ties the competition to the Higher Buildings Policy Review, so the 1997 policy may be amended or replaced. The review's project page also returned HTTP 403 in r1. Check the City's current page before citing it; the brief says the jury may reward justified breaches.

flags.claim: City view cones carry height limits that the tool can read.
flags.detail: The open dataset has 24 polygons and says development within them is height-limited, but it has no height field. Permitted heights sit in the City's per-view pages, which could not be opened. Plan-intersection is only a trigger to check.

flags.claim: OCAP can be named, badged or implemented as a compliance label in the tool.
flags.detail: Secondary sources say OCAP is a registered trademark of the First Nations Information Governance Centre. FNIGC's pages returned HTTP 403. Do not display OCAP-compliant; cite OCAP only as a set of principles and link to FNIGC.

flags.claim: EU AI Act Article 50 labelling duties apply from 2 Aug 2026.
flags.detail: The unofficial text site gives this date but tags the article amended, shows two versions of paragraph 7 and lists a Digital Omnibus document. Timing is not settled and the Act is not binding in BC. The tool uses it only as a labelling benchmark and shows no date to users, or the words as reported; amendments not checked.

flags.claim: Sen̓áḵw developer statements (consultation process, net-zero claim, below-market rents) are established facts.
flags.detail: They are the project's or developer's own statements as reported by senakw.com and Dezeen. Show them as stated by the developer with an as-of date. Sources also differ on timing (S16 gives 2001 and June 2000 for the settlement). Wikipedia's claim of exemption from local height limits cites a 2020 newspaper article and is unverified; no source describes a services agreement with the City.

flags.claim: A downtown plaza renamed with Nation-gifted names (the critic's example: the Vancouver Art Gallery north plaza, with a square name in Nation languages) can serve as a naming precedent in M04.
flags.detail: Not found in r1: the Wikipedia article for the gallery has no such text and the guessed article titles returned 404. City open data does show a downtown plaza with a Nation-language name, formerly Queen Elizabeth Theatre Plaza (S33 record 738), but the record does not say who named it or how. Both leads must be checked in a browser before M04 cites either as a gifted-name precedent.

flags.claim: BC Sans or another open font covers every codepoint in the Nation-name registry.
flags.detail: The BC Sans README says it is a modified Noto Sans with modifications to support Indigenous languages in BC, but names no characters and its licence text was not read. Gentium is OFL-1.1 with automatic diacritic positioning, but First Nations orthographies were not confirmed. Coverage is untested; M05 and M07 test it per string.

flags.claim: The signing certificate in a C2PA manifest identifies the team or an individual.
flags.detail: The spec requires the signer's certificate chain in every manifest (S39 sections 14.2, 14.5). The subject-field rules were not read, so whether a typical certificate names a person or organisation is unconfirmed. The conservative rule (Content Credentials off by default, platform-signed if on) does not depend on the answer.

flags.claim: Zero-tolerance gates (no wording above declared status, no unresolved cultural-content flags, no missing AI labels, no identity-bearing fields on export).
flags.detail: These are platform rules chosen by the team, backed by principles in S01, S04, S22, S28, S47 and the brief's anonymity rule, not by published numeric thresholds. They stay editable and are shown in the team-assumption colour.

flags.claim: The engagement ladder (round 0: four rungs E0-E3; r1: five rungs N0-N4 per Nation) and the phrase-to-minimum-status map.
flags.detail: Team design, not a published standard. The round 0 single ladder is replaced by one ladder per Nation with a counterpart type. Rung names, phrase list and channel locks must be reviewed by a paid Indigenous reviewer before release (see release gate flag).

flags.claim: The as-is workflow of entrants is reconstructed from the brief and typical practice.
flags.detail: Not observed or surveyed; test with two or three student teams before relying on pain points. The round 0 pain point that City sites block automated tools was a problem of the research agent, not of entrants, and is removed.

flags.claim: Effort estimates (about 40 person-days across P07) and the staged scope.
flags.detail: Unvalidated guesses. From 21 Oct to the 13 Nov course checkpoint is 23 days, and to the 30 Nov deadline 40 days, for two students who also build other packets. Core is cut to M01 stage A, M06 and M07; M02, M03, M05, M08 move to v1 and M04 to roadmap.

flags.claim: Whether entrants should contact the three Nations about a hypothetical competition entry, and through which channel.
flags.detail: No statement found on the Buildner competition page or Terms (S34, S47), or on any Nation page opened. The Terms route brief questions through the portal and bar contact with jurors. Default is N0 (no contact; the tool never sends messages). Ask Buildner through the portal before the 3 Nov 2026 Q&A deadline whether any sanctioned channel exists, so that Nations are not burdened by many student requests.

flags.claim: Squamish Nation and Tsleil-Waututh Nation published referral or engagement requirements comparable to Musqueam's.
flags.detail: Still not found in r1. The Squamish home page lists no referral page. The TWN stewardship page (S52) links guides for industry and governments that were not read, and the TWN protocol department page (S53) describes no outside-request process.

flags.claim: Indigenous reviewer sign-off before release: who the reviewer is, who pays, and whether it can happen before 30 Nov 2026.
flags.detail: The critic requires a paid Indigenous reviewer (for example through UBC Indigenous initiatives or SALA Indigenous faculty), independent of the Nations' referral offices and of any juror. Not researched; no person or budget identified. Until sign-off, CULT modules ship only as unreviewed prototypes for course demos and are hidden from entrants.

flags.claim: Spelling of Squamish and Halkomelem strings in the registry (example: Hiy̓ám̓ Housing).
flags.detail: The critic reads the squamish.net page as having no mark on the y; the fetch tool read it with the mark, on both squamish.net and senakw.com. Direct byte-level checking was blocked (HTTP 403). The City API also returned a plaza name with question marks. Every string must be copied by a human from the Nation's page, stored in NFC, and compared by codepoint.

flags.claim: Real-world location of the hypothetical VTC block.
flags.detail: The facts supplied give a hypothetical full-block site in the Central Business District with a rotated north arrow, but no coordinates; the brief PDF was not opened. M06 requires the team to enter a georeference and to say whether it comes from the brief or is a team assumption.

unresolved_relationships: Tower height, form or orientation -> effect on values the Nations attach to views of named mountains (e.g. the Twin Sisters, the Lions) or to Burrard Inlet: no sourced relationship; the tool reports geometry only and must not infer cultural meaning.

Which of the City's 79 UNDRIP actions apply to a private rezoning or competition design, as opposed to City operations: the Strategy PDF was not readable. The Tsleil-Waututh release says only that implementation spans City departments and services.

Design form, motif, metaphor or material choice -> how Nations perceive authenticity or respect: no sourced relationship; deliberately not computed.

Which expression channels (form, naming, pattern, commissioned art) an entrant may open at which engagement status: the lock rule is the team's reading of charter protocols 1, 4, 5 and 9, an Australian-led, self-regulated guide whose fit with Coast Salish protocol is unestablished; no Nation-published rule found.
Share of local material -> cultural or ecological benefit: no sourced threshold in this packet; embodied carbon belongs to the ENER packet.

Whether C2PA signing (keys, certificates) can be reconciled with the competition's no-identifying-information rule: only the certificate-chain requirement was read; subject-field rules were not. Default is off.
Ownership and copyright status of AI-generated imagery under Canadian law: not researched; Buildner only says to check the AI tool's terms.
Whether Local Contexts Hub API terms allow read-only display of Notices in a third-party open-source tool: not reviewed; M05 falls back to link-out.

Who named the downtown plaza with a Nation-language name in City data and by what process, and whether Nations gifted names for downtown public space: the City record does not say; unverified.
Whether the block's real coordinates are fixed by the brief: brief not opened; M06 requires user entry.

case_studies.tool: Local Contexts (TK Labels, BC Labels, Notices, Hub)
case_studies.what_it_does: Lets Indigenous communities attach their own conditions to cultural material and data (Labels), and lets institutions and researchers flag Indigenous interests (Notices: Engagement, Disclosure, Collections Care).
case_studies.workflow_step: Provenance and permission of any Indigenous-derived asset (M05)
case_studies.how_used: Tool shows Notices and community-applied Labels read-only, pulling Notice types from the Hub at run time; records the Hub project ID against an asset. Link-out only until the Hub terms and API guide have been read.
case_studies.strengths: Community-controlled; Notice text cannot be changed; widely adopted in archives and repositories.
case_studies.stops_at: Cannot decide whether a use is permitted, and the tool cannot assign Labels on a community's behalf.
case_studies.license_cost: Icons and template text are copyrighted by Local Contexts; Hub terms and API guide not reviewed.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Prompt the user when an asset is tagged cultural but has no Hub record; remind about missing attribution.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Deciding who holds authority over a piece of knowledge or whether permission is real.

case_studies.what_it_does: Open-source platform where communities set cultural protocols as access levels for digital heritage, with TK Labels built in.
case_studies.workflow_step: Reference pattern for protocol-based access in M05
case_studies.how_used: Pattern only: Nation-held material stays in Nation-controlled systems and is linked, not copied.
case_studies.strengths: Designed with Indigenous communities; protocols are first-class.
case_studies.stops_at: A heritage-management system, not a design or evaluation tool; GPL-3.0 licence means embedding it would impose copyleft.

case_studies.what_it_does: Indigenous-led map of territories, treaties and languages as a starting point for conversation.
case_studies.how_used: Link-out only; the tool never draws territory boundaries as authoritative.
case_studies.strengths: Accessible entry point; openly states it is not an official source.
case_studies.stops_at: Not authoritative, not a consultation tool, and does not define territories.
case_studies.license_cost: API and licence terms not stated on the page opened; unverified.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Which Nation to approach and how.

case_studies.what_it_does: Nation-run interactive map with Elder audio in hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓, photos and a children's book.
case_studies.how_used: Link-out and a prompt to contact the Nation for requests; strings are never scraped or machine-translated.
case_studies.strengths: Nation-authored and authoritative for what it covers.
case_studies.stops_at: Marked under review, not final (round 0 reading; r1 re-fetch failed); no stated citation or reuse rules.
case_studies.license_cost: Site copyright held by the Band; no reuse permission stated.

case_studies.tool: C2PA Content Credentials with IPTC Digital Source Type
case_studies.what_it_does: Open standard for signed provenance records and a vocabulary for marking images as AI-generated or AI-edited.
case_studies.workflow_step: Labelling AI output on boards and exports (M07)
case_studies.how_used: Embed IPTC digital source type and a visible label in every AI-involved export image. Content Credentials are off by default; if on, signed with a platform certificate, because every manifest carries the signer's certificate chain.
case_studies.strengths: Open specification (CC BY 4.0); open-source SDK (MIT or Apache-2.0); identity is optional.
case_studies.stops_at: Labels are declared, easily stripped by platforms, and do not prove authorship or permission; a personal certificate can identify the team and the metadata assertion can carry GPS.
case_studies.license_cost: Spec CC BY 4.0; c2pa-rs MIT OR Apache-2.0; signing certificates may cost money (unverified).
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Auto-fill labels from the tool's own generation log.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Whether using AI for a given element is appropriate.

case_studies.tool: City of Vancouver Open Data: View cones
case_studies.what_it_does: 24 polygons of protected public views, with Queen Elizabeth Park views 3.2.1 to 3.2.4 and links to per-view pages.
case_studies.how_used: Plan-intersection of the georeferenced massing with polygons; lists touched cones with links and marks each as a rule a person must check.
case_studies.strengths: Official, open licence, API access, updated 19 Oct 2026.
case_studies.stops_at: No height field; numbering has gaps, so the set may be partial; zero intersections is not clearance.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Read the per-view documents and extract permitted heights for a human to check (when they can be opened).
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Judgement on whether a view loss is acceptable.

case_studies.tool: International Indigenous Design Charter (ICoD / Deakin University)
case_studies.what_it_does: Self-regulated best-practice guide with ten protocols for designers and buyers of design working with Indigenous knowledge.
case_studies.how_used: Cards named after the ten protocols, each paraphrased in one line and linked; no reproduction of the book.
case_studies.strengths: Names Indigenous-led process, shared benefits and legal and moral permissions in design terms; supported by an international design body.
case_studies.stops_at: Australian-led; workshops in Australia, Denmark, Greenland, Sweden; no Coast Salish contributor named; not a Nation's own rule; where it conflicts with territorial law, law prevails.
case_studies.license_cost: Copyright 2018; reproduction barred without written consent; free to read.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Match declared elements to the protocol they touch and show the relevant card.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Whether a Coast Salish custodian would accept the design.

case_studies.tool: City of Vancouver Open Data: Public art registry (Canada 150+ Indigenous murals)
case_studies.what_it_does: Open registry of public artworks; 17 records mention Coast Salish; records 738, 740, 741 and 744 are 2017 murals from Indigenous artists on downtown sites.
case_studies.how_used: Shows how a City-owned downtown block commissioned Indigenous artists and that several works are no longer in place; also shows a downtown plaza with a Nation-language name formerly known by a theatre's name.
case_studies.strengths: Official, open licence, API, includes commissioning statements.
case_studies.stops_at: Artist names are numeric ids; no identity field; the record does not say who named the plaza.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Whether a precedent's process can be copied.

case_studies.tool: Unicode normalization (UAX 15) with OFL fonts (BC Sans, Gentium)
case_studies.what_it_does: Makes canonically equivalent strings compare equal and lets PDFs show combining marks used in hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ and Sḵwx̱wú7mesh sníchim.
case_studies.workflow_step: Name-string registry (M05) and export glyph check (M07)
case_studies.how_used: Store every Nation-sourced string in NFC; compare after normalization; embed fonts in the PDFs; fail the export if a codepoint has no glyph.
case_studies.strengths: Standard and free; BC Sans is described as modified Noto Sans with BC Indigenous-language support; Gentium is OFL-1.1.
case_studies.stops_at: Normalization does not fix wrong orthography; font coverage and mark placement are untested for these strings.
case_studies.license_cost: Gentium OFL-1.1 (repository page); BC Sans licence not read.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Flag strings that fail normalization or lack glyphs.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Spelling, meaning or permitted use of any string.

modules.name: Per-Nation engagement ledger, claims lint and contact guard
modules.design_question: What can this entry truthfully say about engagement with each of the three Nations, and whom must entrants not contact?
modules.effort: Stage A 2 person-days (N0 statement, contact guard, ban-list lint; unreviewed beta); stage B 3 more (full ladder and lint) after Indigenous review
inputs: Project metadata: site, competition entry flag
Per-Nation declared status, counterpart type and evidence note
Organizer Q&A log (question, date, pasted answer)
Board and narrative text from PRES nodes
Registry of Nation names and Indigenous-language strings (from M05)
outputs: engagement_ledger.json (per Nation: status N0-N4, counterpart type, date, declared-by, evidence note, authorization reference)
claims_lint_report (phrase, location, Nation named, minimum status, pass/fail)
contact_guard_card (juror and channel warning, acknowledged flag, editable portal question)

parameters.name: engagement_status_per_nation
parameters.unit: enum per Nation (Musqueam, Squamish, Tsleil-Waututh): N0 no contact (default); N1 read that Nation's own published material; N2 organizer Q&A answer logged (not engagement); N3 conversation with a person, counterpart type recorded; N4 written permission from an authorized Nation decision-maker for one stated use
parameters.relationship: Higher status permits stronger wording for that Nation only. Engaging one Nation says nothing about the other two, and an individual, artist or Nation corporation is not the Nation's authorized government. Wording above status is blocked.

parameters.name: counterpart_type
parameters.unit: enum: community member, Indigenous artist or consultant, Nation staff, authorized Nation representative, Nation-owned corporation
parameters.relationship: Only a written decision from an authorized representative can support approved-by wording; the other types support only spoke-with wording. Team design; the Indigenous reviewer sets the final list.

parameters.name: claim_vocabulary
parameters.unit: phrase list mapped to minimum status and counterpart
parameters.relationship: Consulted in the duty-to-consult sense is banned for every entry: that duty sits with the Crown and cannot be delegated. Approved-by or endorsed-by needs an authorized-decision reference. Informed-by-Nation-published-sources needs N1 for the Nation named.

parameters.name: contact_guard
parameters.unit: fixed rule plus acknowledgement flag
parameters.relationship: Terms bar approaching or communicating with any juror, on pain of disqualification; brief questions go through the portal's Ask the Jury channel. One juror is affiliated with K̓ESU+CO, so the warning covers jurors' firms too.

parameters.name: referral_reference_items
parameters.unit: count 0-8, reference only, real-project mode
parameters.relationship: Musqueam's eight items describe a real project with regulatory permits and are shown only for real projects. They never prompt an entrant to send a referral, because applicability to competition entries is not established.

parameters.name: nation_name_strings
parameters.unit: list of NFC-normalized strings with source URL, retrieval date and codepoint list
parameters.relationship: Names copied from each Nation's own page keep the Nation in charge of how it is named; typed or machine-translated strings misrepresent people and places. Canonically equivalent sequences must match after normalization.

metrics.name: Wording above declared status, per Nation
metrics.basis: Platform rule: consent and consultation are decided by Nations and governments, so claims of them must be true. The tool checks wording only and cannot verify a declaration.
metrics.method: Phrase lint of board text against each Nation's declared status.

metrics.name: Banned or unsupported phrases (duty-sense consulted; approved or endorsed without authorization reference)
metrics.basis: The duty to consult belongs to the Crown and cannot be delegated to third parties; UNDRIP Arts. 19 and 32(2) are addressed to States. The zero threshold is a platform rule.
metrics.method: Fixed ban list in stage A; extended list after review.

metrics.name: Per-Nation status and evidence note declared at export
metrics.good: yes for all three, with an evidence note for N2 to N4
metrics.bad: undeclared, or N2-N4 without evidence note
metrics.basis: Course rule: every result shows its work.
metrics.method: Check ledger exists and is complete.

metrics.name: Contact guard acknowledged
metrics.basis: Terms bar juror contact; platform rule to make sure every team has seen it.
metrics.method: Check flag before export.

metrics.name: Referral-pack completeness (Musqueam list)
metrics.good: Not applicable to competition entries; shown only for real projects
metrics.bad: Entrant flow prompts, counts or scores referral completeness
metrics.basis: Round 0 marked 8 of 8 as good and verified. The page verifies the list, not that it applies to an ideas competition, and the page does not mention academic or hypothetical projects.
metrics.method: Checklist rendered only in real-project mode.

metrics.name: Indigenous-language strings with Nation source and NFC form
metrics.basis: Platform rule; authority over representation sits with the Nation. Musqueam's own place-names map warns it is not final.
metrics.method: Count registry strings with source URL, retrieval date and NFC match.

modules.method: 1) Each Nation (Musqueam, Squamish, Tsleil-Waututh) has its own record, default N0, with counterpart type and evidence note; N4 needs a document reference. 2) Board and narrative text from PRES nodes is scanned with a phrase list (regular expressions plus stemming, no AI verdict) and each hit is compared with the status of the Nation it names, or of all three if it says the Nations. 3) Duty-sense consulted is always blocked; approved-by and endorsed-by need an authorized-decision reference; informed-by-Nation-published-sources needs N1. 4) The node drafts an editable statement matching the status; at N0 it says no Nation took part in this ideas-competition entry. 5) A contact-guard card shows the juror warning and an editable question for the portal Q&A before 3 Nov 2026. 6) Name strings come only from the M05 registry. The tool never sends messages. It returns export_gate_M01.
visualization: Three-row status ladder, one row per Nation, rungs N0-N4, current rung filled, counterpart-type chip; team-defined rungs in assumption colour
Claims-lint table: offending phrase highlighted in the board text, Nation named, minimum status, link to the rule and source clause
Contact-guard card pinned at the top with a red outline and the Q&A deadline date
Red export banner when any claim exceeds status; grey 'unreviewed beta' ribbon until the Indigenous-review sign-off is recorded in M08
modules.human_judgment: Whether and how to contact anyone, the acknowledgement wording, and whether a declared status is true. Only people can engage the Nations; the tool never does.
modules.limits: The ladder, phrase list and counterpart list are team designs awaiting Indigenous review. N3 and N4 are self-declared and unverifiable; lint catches wording, not intent. No Squamish or Tsleil-Waututh proponent requirements were found, and Musqueam's page does not mention competitions. Whether any sanctioned channel to the Nations exists is unresolved.

parameters.name: claimable_by_entrant
parameters.unit: yes/no per item; FPIC items are no
parameters.relationship: Free, prior and informed consent is obtained by States through Nations' representative institutions. An entrant cannot obtain or claim it, so the matrix offers reflect-on, never addressed, for those items.

parameters.name: programme_mix
parameters.unit: m2 GFA by use tag
parameters.relationship: Commercial, hotel or cultural/civic floor area triggers TRC 92(ii) prompts about who gets jobs, tenancies and long-term benefit from that floor area; no such programme hides the prompt.

parameters.name: decision_category
parameters.unit: enum programme, ground plane, tenure and benefit, naming and art, process
parameters.relationship: Items are routed to the category where a design choice can respond; one item can touch several categories and then shows in several matrix cells. Team design.

parameters.name: attestation_state
parameters.unit: enum addressed, partly, not addressed, out of scope with reason
parameters.relationship: Addressed needs an evidence link on a board or drawing and a claimable item; without evidence the cell shows claimed and joins the open-items list passed to M08.

parameters.name: urban_indigenous_card_set
parameters.unit: separate prompt cards, team-authored
parameters.relationship: The City's implementation committee has urban Indigenous representation alongside the Host Nations, so downtown public-realm and tenancy prompts are kept apart from host-Nation rights-and-title cards. No sourced link to outcomes.

parameters.name: document_status
parameters.unit: enum current, superseded, under review, not opened
parameters.relationship: A badge and as-of date stop users citing a policy that has changed; the 1997 Higher Buildings Policy is under review, and City documents not opened show not opened.

metrics.name: Attestations 'addressed' without evidence link
metrics.basis: Course rule: show the work.
metrics.method: Count cells in state addressed with empty evidence.

metrics.name: Consent or FPIC items shown as addressed
metrics.basis: UNDRIP Arts. 19 and 32(2) place consent-seeking with States; the Crown's duty to consult cannot be delegated. Platform rule that entrants cannot claim it.
metrics.method: Filter claimable=no items for state addressed.

metrics.name: Framework items with no recorded response
metrics.good: 0 (each answered or marked out of scope with reason)
metrics.basis: Platform rule; the Strategy has four themes to cover or exclude openly.
metrics.method: Count empty cells per item.

metrics.name: Cited documents shown without status and as-of date
metrics.basis: Policies change; several City documents could not be opened by the research team.
metrics.method: Check each item for a status badge.

metrics.name: Items without an applies-to tag
metrics.basis: Round 0 critic: untagged items invite entrants to claim duties that belong to governments.
metrics.method: Schema check.

modules.method: A versioned, community-forkable JSON knowledge base lists framework items: citation, as-of date, document status, source URL, decision categories, an applies-to tag (government duty, corporate sector, City operations, design analogy) and a claimable flag; FPIC items are not claimable. The node reads Layer 0 programme tags to pre-select items and shows a matrix; per cell the user records a response, an evidence link and a state. It drafts an outline for the VTC policy reflection with headings, citation links and the user's own notes only; it writes nothing about what any Nation thinks. A separate card set covers urban Indigenous public-realm questions. Items whose source could not be read show document not opened until a human has opened and confirmed it. Colour shows completeness of evidence, not quality.
visualization: Matrix: framework items as rows, decision categories as columns; cell colours grey (open), amber (claimed, no evidence), green (evidence linked), hatched (out of scope with reason), padlock (not claimable); legend says colour means evidence status, not merit
Click a cell: side panel with clause link, applies-to tag, document status and as-of date
Separate panel for urban Indigenous cards, visually apart from host-Nation items
Open-items list with counts per state, no total score
modules.human_judgment: How a policy applies to this design, whether a response is adequate, whether to depart from guidelines (the brief says justified breaches may be rewarded), and what the policy reflection argues.
modules.limits: The City Strategy, Action Plan and Higher Buildings documents could not be opened. Which of the 79 actions apply to private design is unresolved, since the Strategy is addressed to the City. Item tags are team judgments pending Indigenous review. Not legal advice; the brief says its documents are not legal documents.

modules.name: Indigenous design-principle prompt cards with expression-channel locks
modules.design_question: Which published Indigenous design principles should shape this design, which expression channels stay locked at the declared engagement status, and where does the design depart?
modules.effort: 4-5 person-days (10 charter-indexed cards plus 4 team cards)
inputs: Layer 0 geometry and programme tags
Authorship declarations per element (from M05 manifest)
Engagement ledger (M01)
Cultural-content flags (M05)
Precedent do-not-derive lines (M04, when available)
outputs: channel_lock_report (channel, Nation, status, locked or open)
nation_input_needed list for M01 and M08

parameters.name: card_source_type
parameters.unit: enum Nation-published, Indigenous design body, Indigenous-led project, professional body, team-authored
parameters.relationship: A Nation-published card outranks any other, but none exists for downtown towers. The status can be set only on a Nation's own request after manual verification; forks inherit team-authored automatically, so nobody can impersonate Nation authorship.

parameters.name: charter_protocol_index
parameters.unit: one of ten protocol names, paraphrased in one line
parameters.relationship: Each starter card is indexed to one protocol and linked, never reproduced. Protocol 1 says Indigenous stakeholders oversee creative development, so a design representing Indigenous culture without such oversight departs from the charter.

parameters.name: expression_channel_lock
parameters.unit: enum channel: process or acknowledgement, benefit, material as environmental origin, material as cultural claim, form, naming, pattern or story, commissioned art
parameters.relationship: Unless that Nation's status is N4 for the stated use, form, naming, pattern, commissioned art and cultural claims about material are locked; only process, benefit and environmental-origin answers are open. Team reading of charter protocols 1, 4, 5 and 9.

parameters.name: authorship_declaration
parameters.unit: per form, pattern, story or name: designer, Nation-sourced with permission, none
parameters.relationship: Any element declared Indigenous-derived triggers the M05 provenance gate; an element with no declared author is treated as designer-authored and cannot carry Indigenous attribution.

parameters.name: benefit_question
parameters.unit: free text
parameters.relationship: Asking who gains jobs, tenancy and long-term benefit from the commercial programme follows TRC 92(ii) and charter protocol 7 and moves the discussion from imagery to who benefits.

parameters.name: place_name_use
parameters.unit: yes/no and source
parameters.relationship: Using a Nation's place name needs the Nation's own published form; Musqueam marks its map as not final, so names are linked, not copied, and never translated.

parameters.name: deck_review_state
parameters.unit: enum unreviewed prototype, reviewed (scope, reviewer, date)
parameters.relationship: Cards, lock rules and term lists show as unreviewed until a recorded Indigenous-reviewer sign-off exists, and unreviewed decks are hidden from entrants. Platform rule, not a published standard.

metrics.name: Cards with a recorded state (including needs Nation input)
metrics.good: all cards carry a state; needs Nation input stays visible
metrics.bad: cards skipped, or needs Nation input converted into a claim
metrics.basis: Honesty rule; no quality scoring of cultural responses.
metrics.method: Count states in register.

metrics.name: Indigenous-derived elements without declared provenance
metrics.basis: UNDRIP Art. 31(1) puts control of cultural expressions, including designs, with Indigenous peoples; charter protocols 5 and 9 ask for ownership to stay with custodians and for permissions.
metrics.method: Join declarations with the M05 register.

metrics.name: Responses filed in a locked channel for a Nation below N4
metrics.basis: Team reading of charter protocols 1, 4, 5 and 9; the charter is Australian-led and its fit with Coast Salish protocol is unestablished.
metrics.method: Join channel selections with the M01 ledger.

metrics.name: Cards labelled Nation-published without a Nation-initiated verification record
metrics.basis: On a forkable platform the label could be faked; the tool also must not solicit Nations.
metrics.method: Check verification field.

modules.method: A YAML deck. Ten starter cards are indexed to the charter's ten protocols, each paraphrased in one line and linked, because the book bars reproduction; four team-authored cards cover benefit, place names, what the team will not do, and a static do-not-derive-form-from card (standing in until M04 exists). Each card has a prompt, a source badge, a what-the-tool-can-check line and a what-only-people-or-Nations-can-answer line. Users answer in free text and choose one of four states: not considered, considering, responded with evidence, needs Nation input. The channel selector locks form, naming, pattern and commissioned art unless the declared status for that Nation is N4 for that use. Cards on provenance call M05; cards on land, water and views call M06. No numeric aggregation.
visualization: Kanban board of cards in four columns (not considered, considering, responded with evidence, needs Nation input)
Source badge colour by type (Nation, Indigenous design body, professional body, team); locked padlock reserved for verified Nation cards, none today
Channel selector with padlock icons on locked channels and the reason shown
No radar chart and no totals; per-column counts shown only as a plain list
modules.human_judgment: All of it: which principles apply, how to read them, what to change in the design, and when to stop and ask the Nations. The tool only prompts and records.
modules.limits: No Nation-published design guideline for tall buildings was found. The charter is an Australian-led, self-regulated guide; its workshops were in Australia, Denmark, Greenland and Sweden, with a Montreal launch panel, and no Coast Salish contributor is named. Where it conflicts with territorial law, law prevails. Cards are prompts, not approvals, and carry that label.

modules.name: Nation-led and downtown public-realm precedent library
modules.design_question: What can entrants learn from Nation-led developments and downtown public-realm precedents about process, tenure, scale and naming, and what must not be copied?
inputs: Layer 0 tower height, storeys, tower count, GFA by use
Floor-to-floor height (if supplied) to convert metres to storeys
Engagement ledger (M01)
outputs: precedent_facts.json (value, unit, source, as-of date, fact type)
do_not_derive_form_from list for M03 and M08

parameters.name: land_tenure_and_authority
parameters.unit: enum Nation reserve land, Nation plus Crown corporation under City rezoning, City-owned downtown block, hypothetical City-zoned block
parameters.relationship: Who holds decision power over the land sets which approvals and governments apply, so a precedent on Nation-controlled reserve land cannot show what a City rezoning would accept.

parameters.name: scale_storeys
parameters.unit: storeys
parameters.relationship: Precedent heights are in storeys (Sen̓áḵw tallest 58; Jericho sentinels 49) while the competition range is in metres; the tool converts only when floor-to-floor height is supplied, so comparisons do not rest on a guessed ratio.

parameters.name: cultural_expression_channel
parameters.unit: enum process, commissioned art, material, form, naming
parameters.relationship: At Sen̓áḵw expression is described through a Cultural Working Group, Squamish artists, copper facades and tower concepts; each channel needs a different party's authority, so copying a form does not copy the process behind it.

parameters.name: do_not_derive_form_from
parameters.unit: text per precedent
parameters.relationship: Sen̓áḵw describes forms inspired by Coast Salish motifs, longhouses and salmon; those are the Squamish project's own choices. Every precedent carries this line because an entrant cannot borrow the authority behind a form.

parameters.name: downtown_public_realm_precedent
parameters.unit: record: site, tenure, decision-maker, how the work or name arose, in place or removed
parameters.relationship: Downtown precedents show commissioning and naming on City-owned public space, closer to the competition block than reserve land. The City record names the commissioning programme but not who named the plaza, so naming stays unverified.

parameters.name: ownership_and_benefit_model
parameters.unit: enum Nation-owned, Nation-led joint venture, partnership
parameters.relationship: Nation ownership means development returns flow to the Nation, which speaks to TRC 92(ii) long-term benefit; it is unrelated to tower form and must not be presented as a design feature.

parameters.name: as_of_date_and_source_conflict
parameters.unit: date and chip
parameters.relationship: Project facts change (a partner exit in Aug 2025, phase completions to 2033); an old fact without its date misleads. Where sources disagree (settlement 2001 versus June 2000) both values show with a conflict chip.

metrics.name: Precedent facts lacking source or as-of date
metrics.basis: Course rule; some developer claims are unverified.
metrics.method: Validate dataset.

metrics.name: Comparability flags acknowledged before a precedent is cited
metrics.unit: flags acknowledged of flags raised (tenure, authority, scale, programme)
metrics.bad: precedent cited as justification with any flag unacknowledged
metrics.basis: Sen̓áḵw is reserve land, Jericho is a City rezoning with a Crown corporation, and a downtown plaza is City-owned; none equals the hypothetical block.
metrics.method: Compare user tags with each precedent.

metrics.name: Developer statements shown as stated, not as fact
metrics.basis: Consultation process and net-zero claims come from the developer's own pages.
metrics.method: Check fact-type tag.

metrics.name: Source conflicts shown with a single value
metrics.basis: S16 gives two dates for the settlement; showing one hides the conflict.
metrics.method: Dataset check for conflict tags.

modules.method: A curated JSON dataset holds precedent facts, each with value, unit, source id, as-of date and a type (verified fact, developer statement, news report, source conflict). The node pulls the user's massing statistics from Layer 0 and plots them next to the precedents on shared axes (storeys, tower count, programme mix). It raises comparability flags for land tenure, authority, scale and programme and requires the user to acknowledge each before a precedent can be cited. Lessons are written as questions by the team and labelled team-authored. Every precedent has a do-not-derive-form-from line; the Sen̓áḵw services-agreement and height-limit fields stay marked unverified. Downtown precedents come from City open data and are checked in a browser before use.
visualization: Side-by-side elevation strips: each precedent drawn to a storeys scale, the user's tower in the same strip only when floor-to-floor height is known
Comparability matrix (tenure, authority, scale, programme) with equal-sign and not-equal icons
Fact cards with source chip, as-of date, a developer-statement tag and a source-conflict chip; no ranking or score
Downtown precedent cards with tenure, decision-maker and in-place or removed status
modules.human_judgment: Whether a lesson transfers, how to describe a Nation's intentions (the tool does not), and whether to cite a precedent at all.
modules.limits: Facts come from public secondary sources and project websites; City documents were not opened. Jericho figures come from news reports of a policy statement. Sen̓áḵw's reserve status differs from the hypothetical block, so scale comparisons say little about approvals. The downtown naming precedent is unverified and the City record does not say who named the plaza.

modules.name: Cultural-content, appropriation and data-sovereignty guardrail gate
modules.design_question: Does any asset, prompt, reference image or sentence use, imitate or generate Indigenous cultural material or data without a recorded source and permission?
inputs: Asset manifest (images, models, textures, text) with source, licence and declared authorship
Reference-image uploads
AI-generation requests (prompt, model, user)
User-declared permission records
Board text (for borrowed-form phrase scan)
outputs: name_string_registry for M01 (NFC, codepoints, source URL, retrieval date)

parameters.name: cultural_content_flag
parameters.unit: human-set tag per asset, with keyword assist
parameters.relationship: A flag moves an asset from design material to cultural material, which then needs a source and permission record before it can appear on a board.

parameters.name: permission_record
parameters.unit: granted-by, date, scope, label or agreement reference
parameters.relationship: A narrower permission (for example non-commercial or community use only) than the intended use blocks export; conditions come from the community's own labels or agreements.

parameters.name: generation_policy
parameters.unit: fixed rule: Indigenous motif, pattern or sacred-image generation is refused
parameters.relationship: Machine generation of Indigenous motifs removes authorship, protocol and permission from the process, so the tool refuses rather than warns.

parameters.name: borrowed_form_phrase_list
parameters.unit: advisor-curated phrase list; hits are amber, not blocked
parameters.relationship: In tower entries the usual failure is a borrowed form or metaphor, not a pattern file. A hit asks the team to show who authorised the reference; Sen̓áḵw's forms are the Squamish project's own, and an entrant cannot borrow that authority.

parameters.name: reference_image_gate
parameters.unit: per upload: source, licence, flag, permission record
parameters.relationship: A reference image can carry Indigenous work into a render with no prompt text, so image-to-image use of a flagged or unrecorded reference is blocked until a permission record exists.

parameters.name: nation_held_data_mode
parameters.unit: link-out only or copied
parameters.relationship: Nation-held data (maps, audio, place names) is linked, not copied, so possession stays with the Nation; a Nation page marked under review is never cached.

parameters.name: label_display
parameters.unit: Notices shown; Labels shown only if applied by the community in the Hub
parameters.relationship: Labels are applied by communities and Notices by institutions or researchers; the tool may display either but never assigns or edits them, and shows link-out only until the Hub terms have been read.

parameters.name: string_normalization_and_fonts
parameters.unit: NFC form, codepoint list, glyph coverage in embedded export fonts
parameters.relationship: Nation-language strings use combining marks, so equivalent sequences can differ in codepoints. NFC storage and normalized comparison keep lint matches reliable; embedded fonts that cover the glyphs prevent missing-glyph boxes on boards.

metrics.name: Unresolved cultural-content flags at export
metrics.basis: Platform rule derived from UNDRIP Art. 31(1) and CARE Authority to control.
metrics.method: Count flagged assets without a matching permission record.

metrics.name: Indigenous-motif generation requests fulfilled
metrics.basis: Guardrail: the platform must not generate Indigenous motifs or art.
metrics.method: Blocked-action log review.

metrics.name: Flagged or unrecorded reference images used in generation
metrics.basis: Round 0 critic: image-to-image is a second path past the prompt check.
metrics.method: Join generation log with the reference-image register.

metrics.name: Borrowed-form phrase hits without a human note at export
metrics.basis: Hits are prompts for review; the list is team-made and unreviewed, so no hit is treated as a verdict and absence of a hit is not clearance.
metrics.method: Lint board text; check each hit for a note.

metrics.name: Assets with creator's Indigenous identity inferred by the tool
metrics.basis: UNDRIP Art. 33(1): identity is the person's or Nation's to state. The City public-art dataset holds artists as numeric ids and has no identity field.
metrics.method: Audit tags: only human-entered, source-cited values allowed.

metrics.name: Nation-held data copied into the project
metrics.basis: OCAP possession principle; the OCAP trademark steward's page was not opened, so no compliance claim is made.
metrics.method: Manifest check on source type.

metrics.name: Registry strings not in NFC or lacking a glyph in the embedded font
metrics.basis: Unicode: equivalent strings can differ in codepoints; font coverage for these strings is untested.
metrics.method: Normalize and compare; map each codepoint to a glyph in the embedded fonts; a person checks mark placement visually.

modules.method: 1) Every asset, including uploaded reference images, enters a manifest with hash, source URL, licence, author, AI-use field and declared authorship. 2) A human sets the cultural-content flag; keyword assist only suggests. 3) A flagged asset needs a permission record (who granted, scope, date, label or agreement reference) before the gate turns green. 4) AI prompts and reference images are checked against an editable, advisor-curated term list; Indigenous motif, pattern or sacred-image generation is refused with a clause link and logged. 5) Board text is scanned for borrowed-form phrases; hits are amber for human review. 6) Nation-held layers are stored as URL plus retrieval date, never cached. 7) Registry strings are stored in NFC and glyph-checked. 8) Notices and Labels from a Hub project ID show read-only once the Hub terms have been read; link-out until then. No classifier decides whether something is Indigenous.
visualization: Per-asset traffic-light panel: green cleared with permission record, amber flagged awaiting permission, red blocked, each with a clause link
Provenance table with filters by flag, source, licence and reference-image status
Lock icon on blocked generate actions with a plain why-not explanation and a pointer to the Nations' own channels
Amber highlight of borrowed-form phrases inside the board text, with a note field
modules.human_judgment: Deciding whether something is Indigenous cultural material, obtaining and judging permission, reading each Nation's protocols, curating the term and phrase lists with an Indigenous advisor, and reviewing false positives and misses.
modules.limits: Keyword and phrase lists miss intent and produce false positives; absence of a flag is not clearance. The lists are unreviewed until an Indigenous advisor signs off. The tool cannot verify that a permission is real. OCAP and CARE govern data, not design, and OCAP is a registered mark whose terms were not read. Local Contexts API terms were not reviewed.
