modules.name: City in Nature and skyline identity prompts with georeferenced view geometry
modules.design_question: Where is the block, what does the design do for public views to mountains and water, and how are skyline, nature and local materials shown, not asserted?
modules.effort: Georeference and prompt cards 2 person-days (core); view geometry 5 days (may slip to v1)
inputs: Layer 0 tower geometry, heights, public-space tags
Site boundary, the labelled directions on the VTC site plan (rotated north arrow) and the user's georeference
Context massing: existing and approved towers (SITE)
City view-cone polygons (open data)
User-placed viewpoints tagged public or private amenity
Declared materials with origin, planting palette and water features
outputs: view_azimuth_report.json (per viewpoint, public and private separate, baseline vs proposal, degrees)
prompt-card answers to M03, M08 and PRES (QE Park skyline view, ground-level perspectives)

parameters.name: site_georeference
parameters.unit: lat/lon of a block corner, grid rotation in degrees, source (brief or team assumption)
parameters.relationship: The block is hypothetical but cone polygons and bearings are real. Placement decides which cones the massing touches and which bearings apply, so cone and azimuth outputs stay blocked until it is set, and it is printed on every output.

parameters.name: viewpoint_set
parameters.unit: points (x, y, eye height) tagged public or private amenity
parameters.relationship: Public-realm points carry the City in Nature and view-protection argument; terraces and typical floors are private amenity views, reported separately. Higher points see more azimuth; ground points depend on podium height and tower spacing.

parameters.name: target_bearing_ranges
parameters.unit: degrees from site-plan labels
parameters.relationship: The brief's north arrow is rotated against the street grid, so bearings come from the site plan's labelled directions (Stanley Park, BC Place, Entertainment District, Burrard Inlet and North Shore Mountains); assuming true north reports views toward the wrong landmark.

parameters.name: obstruction_context
parameters.unit: set of existing and approved towers
parameters.relationship: More approved towers in the same height range narrow the unobstructed azimuth at public-realm viewpoints, so tower spacing and orientation change the views that public space keeps.

parameters.name: tower_face_width_toward_viewpoint
parameters.unit: m and degrees subtended
parameters.relationship: A wider tower face toward the Queen Elizabeth Park bearing subtends a larger angle in the skyline view; a slimmer face or rotation subtends less. Geometry, not a cultural claim.

parameters.name: view_cone_intersection
parameters.unit: which of the 24 dataset cones the massing intersects in plan
parameters.relationship: Development inside a cone polygon is height-limited, so an intersection means the City's rule for that view must be checked. The dataset has no heights and its numbering has gaps, so zero intersections is not clearance.

parameters.name: place_and_feature_names
parameters.unit: Nation name and City name side by side, each with source; never translated
parameters.relationship: Names from Nation or City sources keep naming authority with them. The tool shows the names beside a view arc but derives no cultural meaning from a direction.

parameters.name: material_origin_and_nature_declaration
parameters.unit: free text with source
parameters.relationship: A declared origin and an evidence link turn local material and City in Nature from adjectives into checkable statements; no sourced numeric threshold was found. A cultural claim about a material is locked by M03 below N4.

metrics.name: Unobstructed azimuth toward target bearings, baseline versus proposal, public viewpoints first
metrics.good: No net loss versus the context-only baseline, or loss documented with a mitigation note
metrics.basis: No sourced threshold exists; this is an editable team preset that asks for explanation rather than scoring.
metrics.method: Ray cast at 1-degree steps over context-only and context-plus-proposal models, public and private reported separately.

metrics.name: View cones whose polygons the massing intersects in plan
metrics.good: Each touched or nearby cone listed with its City height rule checked by a person in a browser
metrics.bad: Zero intersections reported as clearance, or a touched cone with no checked rule
metrics.basis: Round 0 good was 0. The dataset gives no heights, its numbering has gaps (1-2, 4-8, 11-19, 23-26 and letters C, F, I absent), and plan intersection says nothing about permitted height. The brief lets the jury reward justified breaches.
metrics.method: Polygon intersection in plan using the georeference; mark each result rule to be checked.

metrics.name: Queen Elizabeth Park silhouette reported
metrics.unit: angular width and height in degrees, from user-entered viewpoint
metrics.good: Reported for the viewpoint and compared with the four park cones 3.2.1-3.2.4
metrics.bad: Not produced, or produced from a guessed viewpoint
metrics.basis: The brief recommends a skyline view from the park; the cone ids come from the City dataset; viewpoint coordinates are not hard-coded.
metrics.method: Perspective projection of baseline and proposal.

metrics.name: Georeference set and printed on outputs
metrics.good: yes, with source (brief or team assumption)
metrics.bad: no, or not shown on an output
metrics.basis: Round 0 critic: the block is hypothetical, so every view output depends on where it is placed.
metrics.method: Check stamp on each output.

metrics.name: Prompt cards answered with an evidence link
metrics.good: all cards carry an answer and an evidence link or needs input
metrics.basis: Course rule; no scoring of nature or culture.
metrics.method: Count states.

modules.method: 1) The user sets the georeference (block corner, grid rotation, source); until then cone and azimuth outputs stay blocked. 2) Import massing and context from Layer 0 and SITE. 3) Place viewpoints by hand or auto-grid them on surfaces tagged public; tag private amenity points separately. 4) Ray cast at 1-degree steps (team preset) for context-only and context-plus-proposal models with a mesh acceleration structure; record clear arcs toward bearings from the site plan's labelled directions. 5) For the park view, the user enters viewpoint coordinates and eye height (1.6 m is a team preset); the node renders baseline and proposal silhouettes and reports angular extents. 6) Intersect the massing outline with the 24 dataset cones and list ids and links, each marked rule to be checked by a person. 7) Show prompt cards for views, water, skyline identity, material origin, planting. Names appear only from City or Nation sources, side by side, never translated.
visualization: Plan view: radial wedge per viewpoint, baseline arc in grey, proposal arc in teal, lost arc hatched orange, scale 0-360 degrees, site-plan north arrow used; public viewpoints solid outline, private dashed
Elevation silhouette: baseline outline versus proposal outline with an angular scale bar in degrees
Table of touched view cones with ids, links to the City pages and a rule-checked tick box; the legend says zero rows is not clearance
Georeference stamp in the corner of every output; prompt cards with evidence chips; no radar chart, no single score
modules.human_judgment: Which views matter and to whom, what the mountains and water mean to the Nations (the tool does not infer it; Sen̓áḵw's north-pointing rooftops are that project's own choice), whether a loss is acceptable, and whether a material is local in a meaningful sense.
modules.limits: Layer 0 has no terrain by default, so ridge lines need a DEM. The cone dataset has no heights, 24 records with numbering gaps, and its per-view pages could not be opened. The brief's coordinates for the block were not available. The park viewpoint must be entered from City documents. Geometry ignores weather and season. No validated cultural-significance data exists, so none is computed.

modules.name: Ethical AI, authorship and anonymity-safe provenance ledger
modules.design_question: Can every result, image and sentence show who or what made it and from which sources, with AI use labelled, while a competition export carries no identifying information?
modules.effort: 7 person-days (core scope: identity stripping, AI label and source-id lint first)
inputs: Every node output (metrics, images, text)
Asset manifest (owned here; read by M05)
Contributor handles (pseudonymous, platform mode only)
AI-tool log: model, version, prompt hash, date, tool terms link
Module licences and source ids
Registry strings and export fonts (from M05)
outputs: provenance.jsonld (entities, activities, agents; private, platform mode)
board_appendix.md (AI use, sources, module names and licences only)

parameters.name: ai_involvement
parameters.unit: enum none, assistive edit, composite, generated
parameters.relationship: The declared level sets the visible label and the embedded IPTC term; under-declaring breaks trust, and generated imagery should not be presented as sole authorship without permission.

parameters.name: contributor_identity_mode
parameters.unit: enum platform mode (handles and fork authors kept) or competition-export mode (all removed)
parameters.relationship: Handles give attribution on the platform. For export every handle, fork author and author field is removed from boards, appendix and file metadata, because the Terms bar marks identifying the author's source and the brief bars identifying information.

modules.method: Each node run writes a W3C PROV-style JSON-LD record: output (entity), node and version (activity), human handle or tool (agent), inputs and source ids. Competition export mode then (a) removes handles, fork authors and author fields from boards, appendix and file metadata, keeping the full ledger in the team's private storage; (b) embeds the IPTC digital source type and draws a visible AI label on every AI-involved image; (c) leaves Content Credentials off unless the user turns them on, then signs with a project certificate, never a personal one; (d) writes an AI-use-and-sources appendix naming modules and licences only; (e) checks glyph coverage of embedded fonts; (f) lints for missing source ids, unflagged assumptions, image licence records and human review. Prompts are hashed in the browser. The gate fails if any rule fails; the FALSE ASSUMPTION colour state is preserved.

Corner provenance badge on every result card showing author type and source count
Export checklist with pass/fail rows and a fix link per failure; false assumptions kept visible in their special colour
Before-and-after metadata panel showing which identity fields were removed from each file
modules.human_judgment: Whether AI use is appropriate for each element, accountability for every statement, authorship claims, reading the competition's own rules and tool terms, and the decision to publish.
modules.limits: Labels are declared and are lost when platforms strip metadata; a C2PA record does not prove authorship or permission. The brief's anonymity clause was not read. The EU Act is not binding in BC and its dates may have changed. Buildner has no specific AI policy, so the entrant must check each tool's terms. Canadian copyright treatment of AI output was not researched.

modules.method: The node collects state from M01-M07 and builds a three-column register: claim, evidence and source, status (evidenced, intent only, needs Nation input, out of scope). It also lists the review_state of every CULT module, list and deck; anything unreviewed is hidden from entrants, and course demos carry a prototype ribbon. It generates board text skeletons with mandatory blocks: the per-Nation engagement statement (M01), the AI-use-and-sources appendix (M07), the cultural-material provenance note (M05) and a limits statement. The user rewrites all narrative; the node inserts placeholders, not prose. The export gate refuses to pass if M01, M05 or M07 fail. No metric aggregates into a cultural-quality number.

modules.human_judgment: Writing the narrative, choosing what to claim, any reflection on departures from policy, how to describe the relationship to the Nations, and who the reviewer is and when to release.
modules.limits: A coverage register can be gamed by filling cells with intent-only wording. Criterion wording comes from the supplied brief summary, not the PDF. The jury decides quality; nothing here predicts a jury result. No reviewer, budget or timeline has been identified, so the release gate may keep most CULT modules off until after 30 Nov 2026.
